issues.title: A/B test: drop new users into ONE simple feature on first launch (single-feature onboarding)
issues.body:
## Hypothesis

New users today land in a 6-tab dashboard (parties, bookings, events, inventory, pipelines, social) after a generic 3-step onboarding. The cognitive cost of choosing what to try first hurts activation. Hypothesis: **showing exactly one simple, engaging feature on first launch (everything else hidden behind a single 'See more' link) measurably improves D1 retention and the share of new users who complete a first meaningful action**.

## Idea

After signup/login, instead of dropping the user on `/(tabs)/parties`, drop them on a focused single-feature screen with:
- one clear CTA
- no top tabs visible (collapse into a single 'Explore more →' link in the header)
- the existing onboarding modal disabled for the treatment arm so the feature itself is the onboarding

After the user completes the first meaningful action (or after they tap 'Explore more →'), reveal the full tab bar permanently.

## Experiment setup

Wire this through the existing `ACTIVE_EXPERIMENTS` registry in `tdf-mobile/src/experiments/ExperimentProvider.tsx` (the framework is already there and unused):

```ts
{
  id: 'single-feature-onboarding-v1',
  variants: ['control', 'treatment'],
  weights: [0.5, 0.5],
}
```

- **control:** current behavior (3-step onboarding → full tab bar)
- **treatment:** skip onboarding modal, route directly to one focused feature; tabs hidden until first meaningful action OR explicit 'Explore more' tap

### Primary metrics
- D1 retention (returning user the day after install)
- % of new users who complete a first meaningful action within their first session (definition depends on selected feature — see candidates below)

### Secondary metrics
- Time-to-first-action (median)
- Session length on day 0
- 'Explore more →' tap-through rate (treatment only)
- 7-day retention

### Guardrail metrics (must not regress)
- Crash-free sessions
- Conversion to authenticated user (treatment must not gate signup behind the feature)

### Minimum sample
Run for whichever comes first: 2 full weeks, or 1,000 new users per arm.

## Candidate features for the single 'first feature'

Ranked by my read of 'engaging + simple + already shipped'. **Pick exactly one** for the first iteration; the rest become follow-up experiments.

| # | Feature | File | Why it's a candidate | Why it might not be |
|---|---------|------|----------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | **vCard QR scan/share** | `app/(tabs)/vcard.tsx` | Instant tactile payoff (camera opens, you scan a friend, get their contact). Zero-content-needed: works on day 0 with no data in the system. High shareability — every scan is a viral loop. Physical action feels like magic to a first-time user. | Requires camera permission prompt — risk of denial on first launch. Needs at least two people present to feel rewarding. |
| 2 | **Event RSVP / event detail** | `app/(tabs)/events.tsx`, `app/eventDetail.tsx` | Concrete, time-bounded, social. New users immediately see something happening at TDF and can claim a spot — strong dopamine hit. Easy to surface a curated 'next event' card with one CTA: 'RSVP'. | Empty/quiet weeks would be terrible (no upcoming event = dead first impression). Needs a content-freshness fallback. |
| 3 | **Artist profile creation** | `app/createArtistProfile.tsx`, `app/editArtistProfile.tsx` | Identity-investment hook: users who fill in their own profile retain better (well-documented across consumer apps). Already supported as a first-class action. | Higher friction (multiple fields, photo upload). Could trigger drop-off if not framed as quick. |
| 4 | **Venue explorer** | `app/(tabs)/parties.tsx`, `app/venueExplorer.tsx` | Browseable, visual, low-commitment. Good for users who aren't sure what they want yet. | Most passive of the candidates — low chance of producing a 'first meaningful action' metric to optimize against. |
| 5 | **Booking a studio slot** | `app/(tabs)/bookings.tsx` | Highest-value action in the entire app (revenue-generating). | Way too high-commitment for a new user. Belongs in a later activation experiment, not the first-launch one. |

### Recommended pick: **#1 vCard QR scan/share**

Reasoning:
- The interaction is instant and visceral — camera, scan, contact card, done.
- It generates a viral moment by design (one new user scanning another's vCard is the most natural way TDF spreads in-person).
- It works with zero pre-existing data in the user's account (no profile, no events, no bookings required).
- The only real risk is camera-permission denial; mitigate by softening the prompt copy and letting the user fall back to entering a code manually.

Fallback if camera permission is denied: route to **#2 Event RSVP** instead of dumping back into the full tab bar.

## Out of scope
- Backend changes (this is pure mobile UX).
- Web app onboarding (tdf-hq-ui) — separate experiment, separate issue if we want it.
- Personalized feature picking based on user role/intent — that's a follow-up after we learn whether single-feature onboarding works at all.

## Open questions for review
1. Confirm the metric definition of 'first meaningful action' for the chosen feature (e.g. for vCard: 'successfully scanned OR successfully showed own QR to another device').
2. Confirm we have analytics wiring for D1 retention bucketed by experiment variant. `useExperimentEvent.ts` is already in the repo — does it actually emit events anywhere, or do we need to plumb it through to PostHog/Mixpanel/whatever first?
3. Holdout: do we want a third 'no-onboarding-at-all' arm to isolate the modal's effect from the single-feature effect?

---

Filed by Aria on behalf of @diegueins680. Origin: Telegram conversation 2026-06-03.

issues.title: Backend: broadcast new RSVPs to the headlining artist's fanclub — prerequisite for #128
issues.body:
## Why

Issue #128 (single-feature onboarding A/B test) defines 'first meaningful action' as **'a new user submits an RSVP AND that RSVP is broadcast to the fanclub of the artist playing the event'**. The broadcast is what turns a private RSVP into social proof and is the engagement amplifier the experiment is measuring.

The repo already has fanclub primitives — `FanClubPost`, `validateFanClubPostMutationTarget`, `validateFanClubPostPathId` in `tdf-hq/src/TDF/ServerFanClub.hs` — but **no RSVP-triggered broadcast action**.

## Scope

### Backend (Haskell, `tdf-hq`)

1. **Resolve headlining artist for an event.** Add or surface a helper that returns the artist Party tied to an event. (If the schema already supports multi-artist lineups, broadcast to *every* listed artist's fanclub, not just the headliner — TBD during implementation.)
2. **Resolve fanclub members for an artist.** Existing `FanClub` association table presumably has this; if not, add the lookup.
3. **New action: `broadcastRsvpToFanclub :: RsvpId -> AppM ()`.** On RSVP creation it:
   - Looks up event → artist(s)
   - For each artist, looks up fanclub members
   - Emits **one** broadcast per artist (not per fanclub member — clients fan out on read) recording: `{ kind: 'rsvp', eventId, fanPartyId, fanDisplayName, createdAt }`
   - Respects each member's notification preference (mute / digest / live) — add the preference field if it does not exist
4. **Idempotency.** If a user un-RSVPs and re-RSVPs, do not double-broadcast — collapse on `(eventId, fanPartyId)`.
5. **Anti-spam guardrails.**
   - Max 1 broadcast per fan per event regardless of toggling
   - Optional rate-limit: if a fan RSVPs to N events in a day, batch them into a single 'X RSVP'd to N upcoming shows' broadcast (defer this until v2 if it adds scope)

### Storage decision (call out for review)

Two options for the broadcast surface:

| | **(A) Reuse `FanClubPost`** | **(B) New `FanClubActivity` feed** |
|---|---|---|
| Pros | Zero new tables. Existing validators apply. | Cleaner semantic separation — activity ≠ post. Easier to expire/dedupe automatically. |
| Cons | Pollutes the post stream with auto-generated 'X is going' rows. Existing pinning/hiding semantics may not fit. | New table + migrations + permissions. |

**My recommendation: (B) — new lightweight `FanClubActivity` feed.** RSVPs are notifications, not posts; mixing them risks degrading the post-stream UX. The new table can stay small (event-sourced log + 30-day TTL).

Want @diegueins680 to confirm A vs B before implementation.

### Mobile + web client

- New 'fanclub activity' surface (read-only feed): list of recent RSVPs and other auto-activities, separate tab inside the fanclub view
- Push notification (mobile) opt-in: 'New fan going to {event}' (respects notification prefs above)

This client-side surface is **out of scope** for #130 itself — it lands in #128's implementation PR. #130 is purely the backend RSVP → broadcast plumbing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. POST to the RSVP endpoint by a user not previously RSVP'd to an event triggers exactly one broadcast row per artist on the event lineup.
2. POST same RSVP again → no new broadcast row.
3. Un-RSVP then re-RSVP → still no new broadcast row beyond the original.
4. Fanclub member with notification preference `mute` does not receive a push notification but the activity row still exists in their feed.
5. Backend tests cover all four cases.
6. No regression on the existing fanclub post invariants in `ServerSpec.hs`.

## Out of scope
- Client-side feed UI (lives in #128 implementation).
- Cross-artist deduping for collab/lineup shows (v2).
- 'Top fans' rankings or any aggregation (later).

---

Filed by Aria. Blocks #128 alongside #129.
